questions.question: Which national initiative aims to prevent and control non-communicable diseases such as diabetes and hypertension?

options.text: National Programme for Prevention and Control of NCDs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Programme for Prevention and Control of NCDs**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS)**, which has been recently renamed as the **National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD)**, was launched in **2010**. It is the primary initiative in **India** dedicated to managing chronic lifestyle diseases.

• The program focuses on **health promotion**, **early diagnosis**, and **management** of **NCDs**. It aims to strengthen **infrastructure**, develop **human resources**, and provide **palliative care**. This is the correct option as it directly targets **diabetes** and **hypertension**.

• **Mission Indradhanush** is a health mission launched in **December 2014**. Its goal is to ensure full **immunization** coverage for children up to **2 years** of age and **pregnant women** against **12 vaccine-preventable diseases**. It does not focus on **NCDs** like **diabetes**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

• The **National Digital Health Mission (NDHM)**, now known as the **Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)**, was launched in **August 2020**. It focuses on creating a **digital health ecosystem** including **Health IDs** and **Electronic Health Records**. It is a technological framework, not a clinical control program for **NCDs**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)** is the **insurance** component of **Ayushman Bharat**, providing a cover of **Rs. 5 lakh** per family per year for **secondary** and **tertiary care** hospitalization. While it covers treatment for **NCDs**, it is not a dedicated preventive and control initiative like **NP-NCD**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs)**: These are medical conditions that are not infectious and cannot be passed from person to person. In **India**, **NCDs** are responsible for nearly **63%** of all deaths. The four major types are **cardiovascular diseases**, **cancers**, **chronic respiratory diseases**, and **diabetes**.

• **75/25 Initiative**: Launched by the **Union Health Ministry**, this initiative aims to ensure that **75 million** people suffering from **hypertension** and **diabetes** are put on standard care by the year **2025** through **Primary Health Centres**.

• **Ayushman Bharat - Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs)**: These centers are the frontline for **NCD** screening. Population-based screening for **hypertension**, **diabetes**, and common cancers (**oral**, **breast**, and **cervical**) is conducted for all individuals above the age of **30 years**.

• **Risk Factors**: The **NP-NCD** program specifically targets four major behavioral risk factors: **tobacco use**, **unhealthy diet**, **physical inactivity**, and **harmful use of alcohol**.

• **Global Targets**: **India** was the first country to adopt the **Global Monitoring Framework** for **NCDs**, aiming for a **25%** relative reduction in premature mortality from **NCDs** by **2025**, as aligned with the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)** target **3.4**.

**Important Points__**

• **India Hypertension Control Initiative (IHCI)**: This is a **multi-partner** initiative involving the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, **ICMR**, and **WHO**. It won the **2022 UN Interagency Task Force** award for its excellence in scaling up **hypertension** control within the primary health care system.

• **National Health Policy (NHP) 2017**: This policy emphasizes the need for **preventive** and **promotive** health care. It set a target to reduce the prevalence of **tobacco use** by **15%** by **2020** and **30%** by **2025** to combat **NCDs**.

• **Portal for NCDs**: The government has developed a **National NCD Portal** to facilitate the **real-time monitoring** of screening and treatment data across the country, ensuring better follow-up for patients with **chronic conditions**.

• **Financial Support**: Under the **National Health Mission (NHM)**, states receive financial and technical support for setting up **NCD Clinics** at the **District** and **Community Health Centre (CHC)** levels.
</ul

questions.question: If the length of a wire is doubled and its thickness (cross-sectional area) is reduced to half, what will be the effect on its electrical resistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It becomes four times**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **electrical resistance** (R) of a conductor is directly proportional to its **length** (L) and inversely proportional to its **cross-sectional area** (A). This relationship is expressed by the formula: R = rho (L)/(A) , where rho (rho) is the **resistivity** of the material.

• According to the question, the new length (L') is twice the original length (L' = 2L) and the new cross-sectional area (A') is half of the original area (A' = A/2).

• Substituting these new values into the resistance formula: Rₙₑw = rho (2L)/(A/2) .

• By simplifying the expression, we get: Rₙₑw = rho (2L times 2)/(A) = 4 times (rho (L)/(A)) .

• Therefore, the new resistance is **four times** the original resistance (R_new = 4R).

• **Option 1, 2, and 4** are incorrect because they do not satisfy the mathematical relationship derived from the doubling of length and halving of the area simultaneously.

**Additional Information__**

• **Resistivity** ( rho ) is an intrinsic property of a material and does not change with the dimensions (length or area) of the wire; it only changes with **temperature** and the **nature of the material**.

• The **SI unit** of electrical resistance is the **Ohm** (Ω).

• **Ohm's Law** states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided temperature remains constant (V = IR).

• Factors affecting the resistance of a wire include:
 
 
• **Length**: Longer wires have more resistance.
 
• **Thickness (Area)**: Thicker wires have less resistance.
 
• **Temperature**: For most metals, resistance increases as temperature increases.
 
• **Material**: Different materials (like copper vs. nichrome) have different resistivities.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
The sex ratio in India refers to the number of females per ____ males.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1000**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **sex ratio** is a critical demographic indicator used to describe the number of **females** per **1000 males** in a given population. It is used to measure the extent of prevailing equity between males and females in a society at a given point in time.

• In **India**, the sex ratio is calculated as the number of females divided by the number of males, multiplied by **1000**. This standard is followed by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India** during the decadal **Census** operations.

• The options **1200**, **990**, and **1050** are incorrect because they do not represent the official base unit for demographic measurement in the **Indian** context. The denominator for calculating the sex ratio is universally fixed at **1000 males** in official reports.

• This metric is essential for understanding the **gender balance**, **socio-economic status**, and **health** of the female population. A skewed sex ratio often indicates deep-rooted social issues like **gender discrimination** and **female foeticide**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• According to the **Census 2011**, the national sex ratio of **India** was **943** females per **1000 males**, which showed a slight improvement from the **2001 Census** figure of **933**.

• The **Child Sex Ratio**, defined for the age group **0-6 years**, was recorded at **919** in the **2011 Census**, which was a decline from **927** in **2001**, raising significant concerns about the survival of the girl child.

• Among the states, **Kerala** holds the distinction of having the highest sex ratio in **India** with **1084** females per **1000 males** as per the **2011 Census**. Conversely, **Haryana** recorded the lowest among states at **879**.

• Among Union Territories, **Puducherry** has the highest sex ratio at **1037**, while **Daman and Diu** recorded the lowest at **618** in the **2011** data.

• The **National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5)**, conducted between **2019-21**, reported a sex ratio of **1020** females per **1000 males**, indicating a demographic shift, though this data is survey-based and not a complete enumeration like the **Census**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Government of India** launched the **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** scheme on **22 January 2015** at **Panipat, Haryana**, to address the declining child sex ratio and promote women's empowerment through education.

• The **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act, 1994**, was enacted to stop female foeticide and arrest the declining sex ratio by prohibiting **sex determination** before or after conception.

• Factors influencing the sex ratio include **maternal mortality**, **sex-selective abortion**, **literacy rates**, and **differential life expectancy** between genders.

• The **Son Meta-Preference**, a term used in the **Economic Survey 2017-18**, describes the societal desire for a male child, which significantly impacts the sex ratio in several Indian states.
</ul

• A satellite placed in the **halo orbit** around the **L1 point** has the major advantage of continuously viewing the **Sun** without any **occultation** or **eclipses**. This allows for uninterrupted monitoring of **solar activities** and their impact on **space weather**.
 
• The **Lagrange points** are positions in space where the **gravitational forces** of a **two-body system** (like the Sun and Earth) produce enhanced regions of attraction and repulsion. These can be used by spacecraft to reduce **fuel consumption** needed to remain in position.

questions.question: What has been observed in the past decade regarding earthquakes and subsurface fluids?

Earthquakes are no longer triggered by injection and production

• Over the past decade, scientific observations have confirmed a **substantial increase** in the frequency of earthquakes caused by human activities, a phenomenon known as **induced seismicity**.

• The primary cause of this increase is the **injection of fluids** into the subsurface, particularly the disposal of **wastewater** produced during oil and gas operations.

• When fluids are injected into deep disposal wells, they increase the **pore pressure** within the rock formations. This pressure can counteract the **frictional forces** holding a fault together, causing it to slip and trigger an earthquake.

• Regions that were historically seismically quiet, such as **Oklahoma**, **Texas**, and **Kansas** in the **United States**, have seen a dramatic rise in earthquake activity directly correlated with the expansion of **unconventional oil and gas production**.

**Additional Information__**

• In **Oklahoma**, the number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 3.0 or greater jumped from an average of **1.5 per year** prior to 2008 to a peak of **903 in 2015**.

• Mitigation strategies involve **seismic monitoring**, limiting **injection rates**, and avoiding injection near known **basement faults**.

• Apart from oil and gas, other activities like **geothermal energy production** and **carbon capture and storage (CCS)** also involve subsurface fluid management that requires careful monitoring to prevent **triggered seismicity**.

Although he was a champion for the rights of the lower castes, he was not associated with the **Harijan Sevak Sangh** founded in the **20th century**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

questions.question: Why did Mahatma Gandhi call for a campaign against the Rowlatt Act?

options.text: During the non-cooperation movement, thousands of Indians were kept in jail

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Rowlatt Satyagraha:** Gandhi organized the **Satyagraha Sabha** in **Bombay** to direct the movement. He called for a nationwide **hartal** (strike) on **6th April 1919**, which was observed as a day of **humiliation and prayer** and a protest against the unjust law.

The government responded with **martial law**, which eventually culminated in the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** on **13th April 1919**, where **General Dyer** ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering.
 
• **Withdrawal of Satyagraha:** Seeing the violence that erupted following the massacre and the government's brutal repression, **Mahatma Gandhi** withdrew the **Rowlatt Satyagraha** on **18th April 1919**, calling it a **Himalayan Blunder** because the people were not yet fully trained in the methods of **non-violence**.

questions.question:
In a classroom test, students were awarded +6 marks for each correct answer and -3 marks for each incorrect answer. No marks were given for unattempted questions.

Radhika answered 10 questions correctly and scored a total of 42 marks. How many questions did she answer incorrectly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Marks from 10 correct answers = 10 × 6 = 60

Difference between expected and actual score = 60 − 42 = 18

Each incorrect answer reduces the score by 3 marks.

Number of incorrect answers = 18 ÷ 3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks for each correct answer = +6

Marks for each incorrect answer = −3

Number of correct answers = 10

Total marks obtained = 42

**Formula Used:**

Total Score = (Correct answers × Marks per correct) + (Incorrect answers × Marks per incorrect)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e317aa441e48838d73cf6ca4028420adf7b8eb28fecf161fa3351d07adced617.png] 

⇒ Total marks from correct answers = 10 × 6 = 60

⇒ Let the number of incorrect answers be n.

⇒ Total Score = 60 + (n × (−3))

⇒ 42 = 60 − 3n

⇒ 3n = 60 − 42

⇒ 3n = 18

⇒ n = 18 ÷ 3

⇒ n = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Marking System

It is used in competitive exams to penalize wrong guesses. The net score is calculated as: (Correct × Marks) − (Incorrect × Penalty).

Accuracy vs. Attempts

High attempts with low accuracy can result in a lower score than low attempts with 100% accuracy due to negative marking.

Linear Equation in One Variable

Problems involving scores and counts are typically solved using the basic linear form ax + b = c, where x represents the unknown quantity.</p

questions.question: A hollow hemisphere has an inner radius of 5 cm and an outer radius of 7 cm. Find its total surface area.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a hollow hemisphere = π(3R² + r²)

Given: Outer radius (R) = 7 cm, Inner radius (r) = 5 cm

TSA = (22/7) × (3 × 7² + 5²) = (22/7) × (147 + 25)

TSA = (22/7) × 172 ≈ 540.57 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 540.57 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Inner radius (r) = 5 cm

Outer radius (R) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area = Outer CSA + Inner CSA + Area of Base Ring

TSA = 2πR² + 2πr² + π(R² − r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/617e741ca60242cea7ab80f862a920193c023bd4e95604f8270b7274db0ffd3e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Outer Curved Surface Area = 2 × (22/7) × 7² = 2 × 22 × 7 = 308 cm²

⇒ Inner Curved Surface Area = 2 × (22/7) × 5² = 1100/7 ≈ 157.14 cm²

⇒ Area of base ring = π(R² − r²) = (22/7) × (49 − 25) = (22/7) × 24 ≈ 75.43 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 308 + 157.14 + 75.43

⇒ Total Surface Area = 540.57 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 540.57 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Hollow Hemisphere

The volume of a hollow hemisphere is the difference between the volumes of the outer and inner hemispheres: V = 2/3 π(R³ − r³).

Total Surface Area of Solid Hemisphere

For a solid hemisphere of radius r, the total surface area includes the curved surface and the flat circular base: TSA = 3πr².

Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The curved surface area (CSA) of any hemisphere is exactly half the surface area of a full sphere: CSA = 2πr².</p

questions.question: The average weight of 10 parcels is 1.5 kg. If a parcel weighing 2.5 kg is replaced by a new parcel, the average weight becomes 1.6 kg. What is the weight of the new parcel?

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5 kg.**

⇒ Weight of new parcel = Weight of old parcel + Increase in total weight

⇒ Weight of new parcel = 2.5 + 1 = 3.5 kg

questions.question: A student got 30% marks and failed by 13 marks and another student got 44% marks and gets 15 more than the passing marks. Find the maximum mark in a certain examination?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in percentage = 44% − 30% = 14%

Total difference in marks = 13 (fail) + 15 (pass) = 28

14% of Maximum Marks = 28

1% of Maximum Marks = 2

100% of Maximum Marks = 2 × 100 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Student 1: Marks = 30%, Status = Failed by 13 marks

Student 2: Marks = 44%, Status = Passed by 15 marks

**Formula Used:**

Passing Marks = (Marks obtained) + (Failing marks) = (Marks obtained) − (Excess marks)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/526c487b030280e0d9fbe50356a01324e6447394bf3dbee4af929d22b1180e3a.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the maximum marks be x.

⇒ Passing Marks = 30% of x + 13

⇒ Passing Marks = 44% of x − 15

⇒ 30% of x + 13 = 44% of x − 15

⇒ 13 + 15 = 44% of x − 30% of x

⇒ 28 = 14% of x

⇒ 28 = (14 ÷ 100) × x

⇒ x = (28 × 100) ÷ 14

⇒ x = 2 × 100

⇒ x = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

**__Additional Information__**

Passing Percentage

To find the passing percentage, calculate (Passing Marks ÷ Maximum Marks) × 100. In this case: (30% of 200 + 13) = 60 + 13 = 73. Passing % = (73 ÷ 200) × 100 = 36.5%.

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. This is useful for comparing marks between different exams or students.

Base Change Rule

If a student's marks increase by a% and then decrease by a%, the net change is always a decrease of (a² ÷ 100)%.</p

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 18 days. They worked together for 12 days and then B left. A finished the remaining work in 10 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?

questions.question: Two cars start from the same point. One travels north at 60 km/h, the other travels east at 80 km/h. What is the distance between them after 2 hours?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

North and East directions are perpendicular (90°).

Identify the speed ratio: 60 km/h : 80 km/h → 3 : 4.

Using the Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5), the resultant speed ratio is 5.

Relative speed between them = 20 × 5 = 100 km/h.

Distance after 2 hours = 100 km/h × 2 hours = 200 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 200 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Speed of Car 1 (North) = 60 km/h

Speed of Car 2 (East) = 80 km/h

Time = 2 hours

Formula Used: Distance = Speed × Time | Pythagoras Theorem: c² = a² + b²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5173efd5fab812b2908713d54b41bd27f2e61bdf49473933cc4eca89d8e3c4ab.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ Distance traveled North = 60 × 2 = 120 km

⇒ Distance traveled East = 80 × 2 = 160 km

⇒ Total Distance (D) = √((120)² + (160)²)

⇒ D = √(14400 + 25600)

⇒ D = √40000

⇒ D = 200 km

**∴ The correct answer is 200 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17). Any multiple of these is also a triplet.

Direction Relations

Cardinal directions (North, South, East, West) are always at 90° to their adjacent directions, allowing the use of right-angle geometry.

Resultant Speed

If two objects move perpendicularly with speeds v₁ and v₂, the speed of separation is √(v₁² + v₂²).</p

⇒ Let the third angle be x.

⇒ 65° + 45° + x = 180°

⇒ 110° + x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° − 110°
